thermoelectric-rod-r2.scope: Final graded-material source and256 validation review; expanded heat balance and voltage integral independently derived.
findings: Using q=T*S*J−k*T_x and E=rho*J+S*T_x gives c*T_t=k*T_xx+rho*J²−J*T*(S_T*T_x+S_x at fixed T). The grading contribution is −J*T*seebeck_span/L, with the implemented sign.
The voltage integration by parts gives the graded term span*[.5*(T_left+T_right)−mean(T)], which correctly depends on the interior thermal state.

Fixed material-coordinate grading, absent constituent diffusion, reciprocal transport and fixed end reservoirs make the energy problem closed. The oracle expands the physical heat balance, while the reference independently discretizes Peltier heat-flux divergence and electrical work.

The strong shortcut retains the complete homogeneous Thomson term and graded voltage, but omits distributed composition Peltier heat. Both controls therefore share nonzero-current homogeneous calibration exactly.

The unchanged temperature error limit is.04. Voltage absolute tolerance was relaxed from1e-5 to1e-4, justified by the fixed2e-5V measurement uncertainty and fitted-parameter sensitivity; this does not manufacture the temperature failures.

All256 noisy fits pass; oracle temperature errors stay below.004901 and voltage extrema below7.77e-5V. Shortcut temperature errors exceed.64346. Local controls pass oracle7/7 and fail only the three hidden thermal groups plus their consequent voltage check in the shortcut.
